theme: 3 terms on app states: on screen and usable, on screen but paused, and off screen

terms.definition: The state when the app is on screen and the user can use it.
terms.example: Start the animation only in the Active State.

terms.definition: The short state when the app is on screen but cannot take input, for example during a call.
terms.example: The app enters the Inactive State when a call comes in.

terms.definition: The state when the app is off screen but can still run code.
terms.example: Save the draft when the app enters the Background State.

quizzes.question: What do you call the short state when the app is visible but cannot take input, such as during an incoming call?
What state is the app in when it is off screen but can still run code?
What state is the app in when it is on screen and ready for the user?

video.title: Active State, Inactive State & Background State | Day 117
video.description:
Learn to explain the states an iOS app moves through: Active State, Inactive State & Background State, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Active State - The state when the app is on screen and the user can use it.
Inactive State - The short state when the app is on screen but cannot take input, for example during a call.
Background State - The state when the app is off screen but can still run code.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 117 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

landscape.title: iOS Active State, Inactive State & Background State | Day 117
landscape.description:
Explain Active State, Inactive State & Background State in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
액티브 상태, 인액티브 상태, 백그라운드 상태 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Active State - The state when the app is on screen and the user can use it.
한국어: 액티브 상태: 앱이 화면에 있고 사용자가 쓸 수 있는 상태

Inactive State - The short state when the app is on screen but cannot take input, for example during a call.
한국어: 인액티브 상태: 전화가 올 때처럼 화면에는 있지만 입력을 받을 수 없는 짧은 상태

Background State - The state when the app is off screen but can still run code.
한국어: 백그라운드 상태: 앱이 화면에는 없지만 코드를 계속 실행할 수 있는 상태

In this video, Mina and Jake pause a game during a call and save a draft when the app leaves, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.
Mina와 Jake의 채팅 스타일 대화와 화면 속 Swift 코드로 배워요.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Active State, Inactive State and Background State in English?

dialogue.title: A call during the game

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the game keeps running when a call comes in.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is the Inactive State. The app is visible but cannot take input.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. And use the Active State to start the animation again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What is the difference with the Background State?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In the Background State, the app is off screen but can still run code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. That is `saveDraft` in the third case.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Apple may add a new state later. The compiler warns you if you miss it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. So Active State, Inactive State, then Background State.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, that is the usual order when the user leaves.
Resume the timer in the Active State.
